title: Add OCI catalog mirroring with checksum-verified atomic bundle apply; Rocky Linux node base support
author: Nora Singh
description: Summary: Introduces an OCI catalog manifest and a small CLI ('mirrorctl') to build/verifiy an air-gapped registry mirror and perform checksum-verified, atomic bundle applies. Motivation: customers in regulated environments need deterministic offline bundles with end-to-end integrity validation and safe rollback hooks; existing airgap tooling lacked a machine-readable image catalog and lacked an atomic apply that can be rolled back cleanly. Changes: 1) installer/mirrorctl: new lightweight binary and subcommands (index, mirror, verify, apply, rollback) that produce and consume a catalog.json containing image refs, digests, and file checksums; 2) pkg/installer/atomic_apply: new apply engine that validates image digests against catalog, stages bundle metadata, and performs Helm upgrades with --atomic semantics plus preflight checksum gating; 3) terraform/modules/registry-replication: optional module to create registry replication manifests and S3/GCS index storage used by mirrorctl; 4) helm/redwood/templates: values schema extended to accept imageDigestMapping and bundleMetadata entries; 5) distro-support/rocky: packaging and node-init snippets to support Rocky Linux 9 images (sysctl tuning and containerd config) for customers using Rocky in air-gapped datacenters. Backwards compatibility: existing slim bundle format remains supported; mirrorctl can import older index formats and will generate catalog.json when mirroring. Security: manifests are signed using the existing bundle signing key (cosign) and mirrorctl verifies signatures prior to apply. Testing: unit tests added for checksum verification and staged apply/rollback simulation; end-to-end tests added under tests/airgap/e2e that run a local registry mirror in CI and exercise the apply/rollback flow. Rollout: feature gated behind installer CLI flag --enable-oci-catalog and disabled by default for current customers; documentation added. Related: ENG-3245 (airgap catalog), ENG-3310 (rollback guarantees); SUP-7892 documents a customer issue that motivated checksum gating.

review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Please add a short explanation of why we need checksums in addition to image digests. Also add a unit test that simulates a mismatched checksum during apply.
Nora Singh: Added explanation in docs and unit test in tests/atomic/checksum_test.go that intentionally injects a corrupted file to ensure apply aborts. PTAL.
Priya Nair: Can mirrorctl import older slim index formats? We should provide a migration helper for customers with existing mirrors.
Nora Singh: mirrorctl migrate-import command added; doc section explains behavior and that migrating will regenerate catalog.json with digests and file checksums.
Evan Chen: Minor: prefer deterministic JSON ordering for catalog.json to avoid flaky checksum behavior when re-generating. Suggest using a canonical marshaller.
Nora Singh: Switched to canonical JSON marshaller, added tests to assert stable output. All good from my side.
Tomás Rivera: CI showed an intermittent failure on e2e run due to port conflict; I re-ran the job and it passed. Approving.
release_notes: Adds mirrorctl and OCI catalog manifest support for air-gapped installer; supports checksum-verified atomic bundle apply and rollback; optional Terraform module for registry replication; Rocky Linux node-init snippets for on-prem customers. Feature is behind an opt-in flag. (ENG-3245, ENG-3310).
notes_for_ops: Enable with --enable-oci-catalog on installer; to mirror an airgap bundle: run mirrorctl index --source <bundle> --out catalog.json; mirrorctl mirror --catalog catalog.json --target-registry <registry>; verify with mirrorctl verify --catalog catalog.json --registry <registry>; apply with installer apply --catalog catalog.json --atomic. For rollback use mirrorctl rollback --catalog <catalog.json> --target-registry <registry>. See docs/operator/airgap-mirroring.md for full steps.
security_review: Security review completed: cosign-based signing enforced by default for catalog.json; mirrorctl refuses to apply unsigned or tampered catalogs unless --insecure-allow-unsigned is explicitly provided and logged.
migration_instructions: Existing slim bundles can be migrated by running mirrorctl migrate-import --bundle <bundle.tar.gz> which will emit a catalog.json and optional registry mirror plan. Documented caveats for incremental mirrors in docs/operator/airgap-mirroring.md.
